text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:

-Political pressure on Planning Minister Terje Roed-Larsen from the opposition is growing because of his share option 10 years ago, but an opinion poll shows most people think the affair is a storm in a tea cup and that he should stay in office.
-Shareholders in Norway's offshore and engineering company Aker approved a plan for merging Aker with investment group RGI at an extraordinary general assembly on Thursday.
-Norway could be forced to give up its payroll tax system because it could be in conflict with EEA rules. Currently taxes are lower in rural areas.
-According to Morgan Stanley, Norway's pulp and paper producer Norske Skogindustrier is among the seven most competitive paper producers in the world.
-Ten gambling-machine companies plan to merger and become listed on the Oslo Bourse. The new company will have a turnover of 750 million crowns.

-The Munch museum has failed to find a main sponsor for its art collection. Two years ago the museum started a campaign among Norwegian industry in order to find a sponsor, but so far it has not been successful.
